master_profile_text:
FISHING OS — USER CONTEXT / MASTER FISHING PROFILE

USER
- 27-year-old male, Oregon.
- Experienced fly fisherman, especially interested in predatory trout and steelhead.
- Primary targets: Bull trout and large brown trout.
- Secondary/high-priority targets: summer steelhead, tiger trout, big brook trout, trophy redbands, carp.
- Wants factual, confident, well-cited fishing information.
- Do not invent conditions, regulations, flows, weather, fish sizes, or historical data.
- If data cannot be retrieved, explicitly say so.
- User strongly prefers actual data and useful analysis over generic fishing advice.

MASTER FISHING JOURNAL
The journal is intended to become a long-term angling database, not merely a trip diary.

For every trip, preserve:
- Date
- Waterbody
- Exact/approximate location or named hole
- Start/end time
- Weather
- Air temperature
- Wind speed/direction
- Cloud cover
- Barometric pressure
- Pressure trend
- Moon phase/illumination
- Sunrise/sunset
- Rainfall
- Days since measurable rain
- River flow (cfs) where applicable
- Flow trend
- Water temperature where available
- Water clarity
- Tide for coastal fisheries
- Fish seen
- Fish landed
- Fish lost
- Approximate size
- Species
- Flies/lures
- Presentation
- Productive water
- Wildlife/forage observations
- Important behavioral observations
- Lessons learned
- Environmental/fishing correlations

IMPORTANT:
Environmental data should be retrieved from actual historical sources whenever possible. Do NOT fabricate or estimate historical weather, pressure, flow, rainfall, moon, or tide data and present it as observed data.

Preferred environmental sources:
- NOAA/NWS or reliable historical weather station data
- USGS gauges for river flow and water temperature
- NOAA tide data for coastal trips
- Reliable astronomical data for moon phase/sunrise/sunset

Preferred weather stations:
- Nestucca: Hebo, Oregon
- Metolius: Camp Sherman / nearest appropriate station
- Upper Deschutes: La Pine / nearest appropriate station
- East Lake/Diamond/Crane Prairie: nearest representative Central Oregon station
- Imnaha: nearest appropriate station
- Coastal fisheries: nearest representative coastal station

STEELHEAD TRACKING
Steelhead are a major component of the journal.

Lower Deschutes:
- 5-star personal goal: land a summer steelhead on the swing.
- Track flows, recent rainfall, water temperature, timing, visibility, and fly/presentation.
- Summer steelhead are a major priority.

Nestucca:
- Track both summer and winter steelhead.
- For every Nestucca entry, use Hebo weather.
- Flow is considered particularly important.
- Track recent rainfall and days since rain.
- User specifically wants rainfall/flow incorporated into analysis.

Wilson:
- Track winter and summer steelhead timing.
- User will provide additional timing information later.

TROUT PRIORITIES
1. Bull trout — obsession / highest priority.
2. Large brown trout — highest priority.
3. Lower Deschutes summer steelhead — must land a summer fish on the swing.
4. Huge tiger trout — 4-star priority.
5. Big brook trout.
6. Trophy redbands / Upper Klamath Basin.
7. Carp.
8. Winter steelhead.

MAJOR OREGON FISHERIES OF INTEREST
- Metolius River
- Upper Deschutes / Cow Meadows
- Crane Prairie Reservoir
- Wickiup Reservoir
- East Lake
- Diamond Lake
- Lake Billy Chinook
- Lower Deschutes
- Nestucca River
- Wilson River
- Upper Klamath Lake
- Williamson River
- Sprague River
- Imnaha River
- Wallowa River
- Grande Ronde
- Sauvie Island / Crane Lake
- Oregon coastal jetty/rock fisheries

METOLIUS
- User considers the Metolius a primary bull trout fishery.
- River is spring-fed, extremely clear, and generally very stable.
- User frequently fishes specific named locations including:
  - Dolly Hole
  - Pokenny Hole
  - Aquarium Hole
  - Lower Bridge / Bridge 99
  - Long Jams
  - Tailouts
- User wants to investigate upper-river fishing immediately before seasonal closure, especially October, because of large lake-run bull trout moving upstream to spawn.
- Big articulated streamers are extremely important.
- User has repeatedly observed bull trout reacting to large white streamers.
- User has learned that 10–12+ inch streamers can move fish that smaller 4–6 inch flies do not.
- User has observed bull trout attacking hooked whitefish/trout.
- User has observed bull trout attacking other hooked bull trout.
- Important hypothesis to track: bull trout may respond strongly to streamers that dead-drift, stall, or contact the bottom rather than only actively swung/stripped flies.
- User has observed major short feeding windows rather than continuous activity.
- Tailouts may contain many bull trout at certain times, particularly around evening/night, then appear empty later.
- User wants environmental conditions correlated with these behavioral observations.

IMPORTANT METOLIUS JOURNAL OBSERVATIONS
April 8, 2024:
- User considers this one of his best bull trout days and the day he "cracked the code."
- Caught multiple bulls.
- Used huge ~12-inch articulated, often white flies.
- Several big fish.
- Saw fish chasing other fish.
- Caught whitefish and had bull trout remain nearby and attack a streamer.
- User believes 4–6 inch flies often fail to move the biggest fish.
- This pattern has been difficult to reproduce and appears rare.

May 14, 2026:
- Fished Metolius briefly.
- Hooked whitefish in Dolly Hole.
- Large bull immediately ate/attacked the whitefish.
- Bull went extremely deep into euro rod backing.
- User had to enter water to clear snags.
- Ultimately landed the bull.
- Around 7:30 PM.
- No other whitefish sign noted.

May 26, 2026:
- Fished roughly 2 PM–9 PM.
- Water crystal clear / normal Metolius conditions.
- Pokenny: saw at least two bulls; one repeatedly attempted to eat small rainbows user was catching.
- Dolly Hole: no sign initially until whitefish was hooked.
- ~4:20 PM caught a decent fish on euro setup with heavy jig Lunch Money streamer.
- Shortly afterward caught ~16-inch fish on switch rod with indicator and golden stone.
- Fished hard until dark.
- Around 8:50 PM caught a massive bull in deep tailout on a swung fly.
- Fish made multiple hard upstream runs.
- Barely fit in Fishpond Mid-Length net; estimated >35 inches / 3x net basket length (size estimate uncertain).
- This was NOT a sighting; it was a landed fish.
- Important: user corrected earlier misunderstanding that this was a "giant sighting."

June 15, 2025:
- Pokenny Hole: bull around 18–20 inches at 9:44 AM.

June 16, 2025:
- Dolly Hole: brown trout around 18 inches on a nymph.
- Pokenny: bull around 22 inches at 6:55 AM.
- Roadside deep bucket near campground pull-off: bull around 24 inches at 9:08 AM.
- Saw golden stones on branches.

July 5, 2025:
- Around 9:27 PM caught a thick bull around 24 inches immediately below lower bridge.
- 12+ inch yellow/white brush streamer.
- Also caught a brown trout.

September 2025 Metolius:
- September 23: very productive day, lots of fish/running.
- Large colored-up trout estimated 25+ inches near Lake Creek.
- Another smaller bull upper river around 1:47 PM.
- September 24: bull around 20 inches in Long Jams below Dolly Hole around 10:48 PM.
- Another afternoon session with Michael produced several rainbows.
- User snapped rod.

July 11, 2026:
- Started ~5 PM.
- Checked upstream spot without success, then Dolly Hole by ~5:30 PM.
- Fished until ~1 hour after sunset (~9:51 PM).
- Bull #1: 7:11 PM, 10-inch white streamer / red-wire "Bully" contraption.
- Bull #2: 7:53 PM, basic white-on-white Dolly Llama.
- Lost another small bull after another bull attacked it.
- Strong bull frenzy roughly 7–8 PM.
- Activity then died.
- Walked to tailout and saw many bull trout eyes; described it as insane.
- Next day saw no bull trout in lower tailout.
- Possible otter observed rising.

July 12, 2026:
- Dolly Hole ~4:30–6:45 AM: one small bull on streamer, otherwise quiet.
- Pokenny: moved one bull but no eat.
- Lower Bridge: fished until around noon; no fish seen.
- Aquarium Hole with Chase: moved fish; caught whitefish on nymph, followed by bull trout.
- Dolly Hole ~6:30–10 PM: very slow, one bull observed.
- Repeatedly saw a fish porpoising in same location.
- Other anglers believed these were Chinook.
- Another scarred fish with white patches was also believed to be Chinook.
- User suspects a pair of Chinook may have been present.
- Baby black bear observed.
- Dolly tailout had no visible bull eyes, unusual compared with previous evening.

July 14, 2026:
- Dolly Hole ~9 AM–noon: no fish.
- Around noon Bridge 99: Chase caught ~12-inch bull on spinner with minnow attached.
- Pokenny around 3 PM: caught a couple rainbows, no big bull.
- Aquarium Hole ~7–10 PM: caught two bulls, ~20 and ~18 inches.
- Both on large white streamer in far tailout.

July 15, 2026:
- Dolly Hole ~5:30 AM–1 PM.
- Around 6 AM: ~16-inch tagged bull on swung Sparkle Minnow.
- Hooked a substantially larger bull on switch rod indicator with small caddis Perdigon; fish made hard run and broke off.
- Saw many fish in tailout in morning.
- Fish seemed to move forward into hole as morning progressed, while some remained deep/far tailout under logs.
- Around 10:20 AM activity suddenly increased for ~30 minutes.
- Hooked approximately seven bull trout.
- Landed three.
- Largest approximately 27 inches.
- A ~20-inch bull ate large white streamer; larger bull attacked it and both were hooked briefly before smaller fish came off.
- Alternated 12–14 inch white streamer and 15-inch olive streamer.
- Olive generated interest from two fish.
- User believes hooks are too large and contributed to losses.
- Important observation: bull trout repeatedly showed willingness to attack streamer when it was dead-drifted or even snagged on bottom.
- Fish could appear from nowhere to eat a fly resting near bottom.
- User wants to determine better presentation.
- Fished holes below Dolly with large white streamer and got no eats.
- Lower Bridge ~2:30–3:30 PM: no bulls on large white streamer.

UPPER DESCHUTES / COW MEADOWS
May 24, 2026:
- Fished Cow Meadows.
- Large brook trout present.
- Landed one easy ~18-inch brook trout.
- Jig streamer, Sparkle Minnow / minnow color, worked in logs and undercuts.
- Many looks/eats.
- Estimated ~20 fish landed in ~4 hours.
- Unclear whether any were rainbows.
- Floated lake in pontoon in morning; okay fishing.
- Spooked many fish.
- Could not initially find deep water; fish were holding in weeds.
- Caught one while stripping a leech sight-fishing to a decent brook trout.
- User believes there are large brook trout moving toward Cow Meadows.
- User has interest in timing these fish around late summer/fall.

June/July 2025:
- July 6, 2025: Three Creeks Lake with Michael and Grace. Caught several brookies and rainbows. Decent day. Tons of mosquitoes, mostly not on water.

September 8, 2025:
- Cow Meadows / Upper Deschutes.
- One of user's first times there.
- Very good brook trout fishing.
- Euro rig with jig white baitfish pattern and ~4.5 mm orange hot-head bead.
- Many brook trout, average ~11 inches.
- One nice rainbow ~18 inches.
- Weather sunny and warm.

LAKE BILLY CHINook
April 26, 2026:
- Tried stripping flies and bobbers in lake; no bulls.
- Went up Deschutes Arm.
- Saw many suckers.
- Caught several rainbows, one brown, and one bull around 17 inches.
- Bull caught ~10:50 AM.

SAUVIE ISLAND / CARP
May 11, 2026:
- Crane Lake, Sauvie Island.
- Landed 3 carp.
- Tons of activity.
- Orange woolly-bugger-like fly.
- Fly had no hackle and may have been craw-style.

June 1, 2026:
- Sauvie Island carp.
- Much less activity than previous outing.
- Saw only a few fish.
- Zero hookups / approximately one real shot.
- User wants weather, pressure, moon phase, temperature and environmental data tracked for every carp trip.

NESTUCCA
June 30, 2026:
- Wade fishing.
- Started ~11:30 AM.
- Mostly walked and threw spinners.
- Lower river.
- Pink #2 Blue Fox spinner.
- Moved one jack (~20").
- Landed at least 10 coastal cutthroat.
- Little/no wind, overcast.
- Big corner hole on lower river below bridge produced steelhead.
- Saw approximately five or more bright steelhead.
- Fish interested in spinner after ~1 hour.
- Lost one immediately on hookset with pink #2.
- Changed to blue #3 Blue Fox.
- Landed one steelhead at 6:18 PM.
- 29 inches, 14.5-inch girth.
- Approximate weight should be calculated using an appropriate steelhead length/girth formula, with uncertainty clearly stated.
- Continued until ~7:30 PM.
- No additional fish.
- Checked "Newt Hole" on way out with same spinner, no action.
- IMPORTANT: Use Hebo weather for Nestucca.
- Track river flow and recent rainfall because user believes they are critical for coastal steelhead.

July 4, 2026:
- Approximately 9 AM–6 PM.
- Covered lots of water on foot.
- Mainly spinners.
- Lower river: only one steelhead observed.
- Above CJ's Hole: saw ~3 steelhead and one Chinook.
- Landed one Chinook on spinner.
- User wants flow and recent rainfall tracked for this fishery.
- "Big Corner Hole" below bridge is an unnamed location; user may want to name it later.

IMNAHA / WALLOWA
September 17–18, 2025:
- Fished Imnaha River for bull trout.
- Blue Hole.
- Bull trout fishing was very hot.
- Many bulls.
- Several 26+ inch fish.
- Fish appeared strongly associated with spawning activity.
- Trip occurred under overcast conditions.
- User wants to return despite distance and somewhat rough logistics.
- September 17 fished Wallowa River while driving over.
- Did well on rainbow trout.

BIG HORN RIVER
September 20, 2025:
- Rented boat and floated Bighorn River.
- Very good day.
- Many rainbows and a few nice browns.
- Jerk-stripping a leech over weed beds was highly effective on rainbows.
- User was primarily targeting browns.
- Include this in destination/travel fishing journal.

BELIZE
March 21–April 1, 2025:
- Belize / Caye Caulker area.
- Overall trip was great; fishing was lackluster.
- Lost ~30 lb tarpon at boat.
- Caught a few small bonefish.
- Missed permit.
- Saw/missed opportunity at pair of 150+ lb tarpon crushing flats.
- User considers this an important missed-opportunity trip.
- Future Belize/Caye Caulker trip is a major travel fishing interest.

BAJA / LA PAZ
April 3–8, 2026:
- Six days fishing around La Paz, Mexico.
- Landed approximately 50 roosterfish.
- User's largest rooster approximately 20 lb.
- Friend/buddy landed approximately 55–60 lb rooster.
- 30 lb fluorocarbon straight through was considered key.
- Many pelicans.
- Needlefish bait was a major issue on at least one day.
- Large jacks: three very large jacks landed/encountered.
- One skipjack tuna.
- Buddy caught one mahi.
- User saw only one mahi.
- Many triggerfish.
- Saw bonefish.
- Heard rumors of permit.
- User knows region also has tuna, amberjack, golden trevally, etc.
- Trip coincided with a busy Mexican holiday weekend.
- Roosterfish beaches were very busy, which user believes hurt fishing.
- User observed from social media that larger roosterfish activity increased substantially after departure, along with mahi activity.
- User suspects trip was slightly before peak big-rooster activity.
- User may add more detailed Baja notes later.

COASTAL JETTY / ROCKFISH
June 16, 2026:
- Fished jetty most of day, approximately 8 AM–4 PM.
- Fishing initially slow.
- One fish right away, then several-hour lull.
- Activity increased when tide began coming in.
- Need to retrieve exact high tide from correct NOAA tide station once jetty is identified.
- Caught quite a few rockfish on white/chartreuse Clouser.
- Most were extremely small, around 4 inches.
- User had never seen such a concentration of tiny rockfish before.
- Tide appeared strongly related to increased activity.
- User wants coastal environmental data tracked including tide, swell, wind, pressure, weather, etc.
- Exact jetty location needs to be confirmed.

FISHING JOURNAL PHILOSOPHY
The journal should eventually allow analysis such as:
- Best Metolius bull trout flows
- Best Metolius feeding windows by season/time
- Bull trout response to pressure/weather/moon
- Nestucca steelhead success vs flow and rainfall
- Best steelhead conditions
- Brown trout seasonal movement
- Fly/presentation success
- Fish size vs environmental conditions
- Repeatability of feeding windows
- Which conditions produce trophy fish
- "Where should I fish this week?" recommendations based on user's own historical data plus current conditions

Do not overstate causation. Distinguish:
- Observed fact
- Retrieved environmental data
- Strong inference
- Hypothesis
- Speculation

FISHING SCHEDULE / PRIORITIES
Annual schedule is intended to be WEEKLY, with:
- Primary fishery
- Backup fishery that is on the route home or only a slight detour
- Other options
- Star rating
- Trophy potential
- Personal priority

Important recurring priorities:
- Winter/summer steelhead on Oregon coastal rivers
- Metolius bull trout
- Upper Deschutes/Cow Meadows brook trout
- East Lake trophy browns
- Diamond Lake trophy browns
- Lake Billy Chinook bull trout
- Lower Deschutes summer steelhead
- Upper Klamath and tributaries
- Fall Montana fishing
- April Baja
- May Belize/Caye Caulker
- August Alaska

TRAVEL FISHING
- Alaska August 2026: Katmai Trophy Lodge trip planned/paid, likely Aug 8–15.
- Goals: coho on fly, char/Dolly, Arctic char, very large rainbows (25+ goal).
- Less interested in pink/chum/sockeye.
- Wants manageable float trips; experienced but somewhat rusty.
- Grandfather less mobile and prefers gear fishing.
- Montana fall trip is a major future priority.
- Baja in April.
- Belize/Caye Caulker in May.

OREGON REGULATIONS
- User has uploaded:
  - 2025–2026 fishing regulations PDF
  - Oregon Fishing Regulations 2026 PDF
- These should be consulted for current regulations, closures, seasons, species rules, etc.
- User specifically wants Upper Metolius closure dates verified from the 2026 ODFW regulations.
- User believes Upper Deschutes closes September 30 and wants this confirmed before planning.
- Do not rely on memory for regulations when uploaded official regulations are available.

UPLOADED REFERENCE MATERIALS
- 2025–2026 fishing regulations.pdf
- Oregon Fishing Regs 2026.pdf
- Sankovich_2020_ImnahaRiverWeir_2019annualreportl.pdf
- Fly fishing (for AI) 6-15.pdf

STYLE FOR FISHING OS
- Direct.
- Factual.
- Confident when evidence supports confidence.
- Cite sources.
- No generic filler.
- No pretending to have retrieved data.
- If an environmental value is unavailable, say "not retrieved" or "unavailable."
- User wants useful insights, not repeated summaries.
- When analyzing a fishing trip, prioritize actionable patterns and explain confidence.
- User wants environmental data automatically attached to every new journal entry.
- Historical trips should be backfilled in chronological order when reliable archived data can be retrieved.
- Do not repeatedly ask whether to proceed with the backfill; proceed when tools/data allow.

journal.title: Wickiup Spring Arm — Big Browns
journal.observed: Hundreds of fish stacked into a spring-fed arm under low water. Springs made water very murky. Larger browns were close to the bank in roughly 1 ft of water and sat until spooked by light. Many 12–22 inch browns farther out.
journal.result: A 24+ inch brown and a similarly large rainbow were caught; streamer produced the large brown during a short morning window.
journal.hypothesis: A bobber-and-egg presentation may work for large bank-holding browns, but the shallow water makes drift/presentation critical.

journal.title: Metolius — Bull Trout Dead-Drift Response
journal.observed: On July 15, 2026, bull trout repeatedly attacked streamers when dead-drifted or resting/snagged near bottom. Fish could appear from nowhere to eat a fly near bottom.
journal.hypothesis: Bull trout may respond strongly to stalled/dead-drifted bottom-adjacent streamers rather than only active swings.

journal.title: Nestucca — Steelhead + Rainfall/Flow Tracking
journal.observed: June 30, 2026 produced a 29 in steelhead with 14.5 in girth after a pink #2 broke off and a blue #3 was used.
journal.analysis_rule: Always attach Hebo weather, river flow and recent rainfall/days since rain when available.

master_note: Why I fish — I keep coming back to the same question: why I choose to pursue fly fishing. Is it the challenge, the constant fly fishing is a vessel for exploration that will lead you across the world. The pursuit of the unknown and the hope of the next adventure. I often stay up late at night getting worked up over the prospect of exploring new waters. I think the draw for me comes from the constant growth that persists with challenging yourself and exploring these new places and cultures. Constant evolution and innovation of gear, both personally and in the industry, keeps the age old tradition fresh.
